report.incidentSummary: Starting at 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC) on 2026-10-16, auth-service OTP verification success rate dropped abruptly from ~97.4% to ~70%, impacting roughly 25-30% of user login attempts. Investigation revealed that internal infrastructure, message queues, cache keyspace, and synchronous SMS handoffs from notification-service to sms-provider remained healthy. The symptoms and failure characteristics match historical carrier-side SMS delivery latency issues (PIR-1602), where downstream telecom carrier delivery delays exceed the recently shortened 240-second OTP expiration window (CHG-48224), resulting in expired code rejections by auth-service.
report.rootCauseStatement: Downstream SMS provider carrier-route delivery delays caused OTP SMS messages to be delivered to users after the configured 240-second validity window (reduced from 300s under CHG-48224), causing auth-service to reject valid user-submitted OTP codes as expired despite successful synchronous dispatch acceptance (HTTP 202) by the SMS aggregator.

hypotheses.cause: External SMS provider routing degradation or carrier delivery delays (analogous to PIR-1602) caused OTP SMS messages to arrive after the configured 240s expiration window (CHG-48224), causing users to submit valid codes that auth-service rejects as expired.
hypotheses.rationale: Internal systems (cache, notification-service, message-queue, and auth-service latency) were completely stable throughout the incident. SMS dispatches succeeded synchronously with HTTP 202 at notification-service without spikes in send failures, matching PIR-1602 where carrier delays caused OTPs to arrive after expiration.

hypotheses.cause: Infrastructure change CHG-48221 (upgrading log-shipper agent to v3.0 on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC) caused node-level disruption or silent container degradation on auth-service instances.
hypotheses.rationale: auth-service p50 and p95 request latencies remained completely stable at ~60ms and ~297ms respectively across 04:54 UTC and 05:10 UTC, and logs showed no crash events, container restarts, or resource exhaustion errors.

facts.statement: auth-service otp_success_rate plummeted from ~97.4% to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC and settled around 68-72% through 07:00 UTC.
auth-service latency_p95_ms (mean 297.3ms) and latency_p50_ms (mean 59.7ms) remained stable without any spikes around the 04:54 UTC log-shipper deployment or the 05:10 UTC incident onset.
notification-service latency_p95_ms remained steady between 110.8ms and 126.2ms, and sms_send_failures stayed at baseline levels of 2.2-4.8 failures/min throughout the entire window.
message-queue consumer lag was stable at ~2.08s and notifications queue depth remained steady at ~110 messages, showing no queue congestion.
notification-service logs show that all sampled OTP SMS dispatches were synchronously accepted by sms-provider with HTTP status 202.
Cache memory utilization remained stable at ~62%, cache evictions per minute remained flat at ~35.7 count/min, and session cache hit rate remained elevated at ~94.9%.
auth-service configuration change CHG-48224 reduced otp.expiry_s from 300 seconds to 240 seconds on 2026-10-14.
Historical incident PIR-1602 documented SMS provider routing degradation leading to 2-5 minute SMS delivery latency, resulting in dropped OTP login completion.

inferences.statement: Because notification-service synchronously delivers OTP requests to sms-provider without queue backlog or API rejections, the delivery delay occurs downstream at the SMS aggregator or telecom carrier level.

The sharp drop in otp_success_rate without corresponding spikes in auth-service 5xx errors or request latency indicates that OTP verification calls are logically rejected due to expired or invalid tokens submitted by users who received SMS late.
The reduction in OTP expiry to 240s under CHG-48224 decreased tolerance for carrier transit delays, causing telecom routing latency of 4+ minutes to translate directly into verification failures.

assumptions.statement: Approximately 25-30% of user logins route through affected telecom carrier circles experiencing SMS transit latency exceeding 240 seconds.
auth-service treats expired OTP code submissions as validation failures returning 200 or 4xx responses rather than internal 5xx server errors.

timeline.event: CHG-48224 applied to auth-service, reducing otp.expiry_s from 300s to 240s.
CHG-48221 completed log shipper upgrade (v2.8 to v3.0) on auth-service node pool.

confidence.rationale: All internal application components (auth-service latency, cache hit rates/evictions, notification queue depths and dispatch latency) were definitively eliminated as causes. Outbound SMS API handoffs succeed with HTTP 202, and the exact failure pattern matches PIR-1602 where carrier delivery latency breached the OTP expiry threshold.

recommendedActions.action: Fail over OTP SMS dispatch traffic to the secondary SMS provider route or trigger multi-carrier routing via notification-service configuration.
recommendedActions.rationale: Historical incident PIR-2004 and PIR-1602 demonstrated that rerouting traffic away from degraded primary provider routes restores normal delivery latency and login success.
recommendedActions.verification: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate to verify return to normal baseline (>95%).

recommendedActions.action: Temporarily increase auth-service otp.expiry_s configuration back from 240 seconds to 300 or 360 seconds.
recommendedActions.rationale: Broadening the expiration window absorbs transient carrier delivery latency and allows delayed SMS codes to still be verified successfully.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify otp.expiry_s config update in auth-service and observe reduction in OTP verification failure rate.

recommendedActions.action: Implement granular DLR latency tracking and export distinct metrics for OTP validation failures (e.g., otp_expired vs otp_mismatched) in auth-service.
recommendedActions.rationale: Direct telemetry will allow immediate automated detection of carrier delivery delays versus authentication brute-force or application errors.

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.85 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC) on 2026-10-16, auth-service OTP verification success rate dropped abruptly from ~97.4% to ~70%, impacting roughly 25-30% of user login attempts. Investigation revealed that internal infrastructure, message queues, cache keyspace, and synchronous SMS handoffs from notification-service to sms-provider remained healthy. The symptoms and failure characteristics match historical carrier-side SMS delivery latency issues (PIR-1602), where downstream telecom carrier delivery delays exceed the recently shortened 240-second OTP expiration window (CHG-48224), resulting in expired code rejections by auth-service.

**Root cause:** Downstream SMS provider carrier-route delivery delays caused OTP SMS messages to be delivered to users after the configured 240-second validity window (reduced from 300s under CHG-48224), causing auth-service to reject valid user-submitted OTP codes as expired despite successful synchronous dispatch acceptance (HTTP 202) by the SMS aggregator.

## Hypotheses
1. **External SMS provider routing degradation or carrier delivery delays (analogous to PIR-1602) caused OTP SMS messages to arrive after the configured 240s expiration window (CHG-48224), causing users to submit valid codes that auth-service rejects as expired.** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.85, supported

   - Internal systems (cache, notification-service, message-queue, and auth-service latency) were completely stable throughout the incident. SMS dispatches succeeded synchronously with HTTP 202 at notification-service without spikes in send failures, matching PIR-1602 where carrier delays caused OTPs to arrive after expiration.
2. **Infrastructure change CHG-48221 (upgrading log-shipper agent to v3.0 on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC) caused node-level disruption or silent container degradation on auth-service instances.** — `auth-service`, infrastructure_failure, confidence 0.15, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_7, ev_21, ev_29] · Contradicting: [ev_34, ev_36, ev_37]
   - auth-service p50 and p95 request latencies remained completely stable at ~60ms and ~297ms respectively across 04:54 UTC and 05:10 UTC, and logs showed no crash events, container restarts, or resource exhaustion errors.

## Facts
- auth-service otp_success_rate plummeted from ~97.4% to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC and settled around 68-72% through 07:00 UTC. [ev_1, ev_27]
- auth-service latency_p95_ms (mean 297.3ms) and latency_p50_ms (mean 59.7ms) remained stable without any spikes around the 04:54 UTC log-shipper deployment or the 05:10 UTC incident onset. [ev_34, ev_37]
- notification-service latency_p95_ms remained steady between 110.8ms and 126.2ms, and sms_send_failures stayed at baseline levels of 2.2-4.8 failures/min throughout the entire window. [ev_2, ev_3]
- message-queue consumer lag was stable at ~2.08s and notifications queue depth remained steady at ~110 messages, showing no queue congestion. [ev_4, ev_10]
- notification-service logs show that all sampled OTP SMS dispatches were synchronously accepted by sms-provider with HTTP status 202. [ev_35]

- The reduction in OTP expiry to 240s under CHG-48224 decreased tolerance for carrier transit delays, causing telecom routing latency of 4+ minutes to translate directly into verification failures. [ev_1, ev_6, ev_26, ev_29]

- Approximately 25-30% of user logins route through affected telecom carrier circles experiencing SMS transit latency exceeding 240 seconds.
- auth-service treats expired OTP code submissions as validation failures returning 200 or 4xx responses rather than internal 5xx server errors.
